note: Per-ISO holdout markers gating CLAUDE.md rule 22. TWO INDEPENDENT MARKER BLOCKS (owner decision 2026-07-31), selected by the TIER of the year being touched — the gates were previously tier-agnostic, so a single `complete` entry authorized the iterable 2022 validation ladder and the touch-once 2019/H1-2026 locked test alike. `complete` = VALIDATION tier (2022 and its backward ladder 2018/2020/2021): iterable by design, model-SELECTION evidence, NOT training and never quotable as a certified out-of-sample skill number. `final` = LOCKED-TEST tier (2019, H1-2026): touch-once ever, scored EXACTLY ONCE per ISO with the frozen keeper config, recorded whatever it is, and no calibration change may respond to it. An ISO in `complete` but not `final` may spend its validation ladder and NOTHING else. ABSENCE FROM `final` IS NOT A GRANT AND NOT AUTOMATICALLY A PENDING GRANT — read the ISO's `locked_test` note: it distinguishes 'never authorized' from 'authorized once, SPENT, never re-grantable'. Rule 22 splits two orthogonal channels: (1) DATA INTAKE for any out-of-training year is allowed any time, for any ISO, under explicit session-logged owner authorization, validated no-LP only (byte-identity / loader-resolvability — never a dispatch solve); see `intake_log`; it needs NO marker. (2) SOLVE, SCORE and DASHBOARD REGISTRATION of an out-of-training year need that year's TIER marker. The HOLDOUT SPEND FREEZE (frontend/data/backcast/holdout-freeze.json) outranks BOTH blocks and is checked first: while it is active no out-of-training year may be solved for any ISO, marker or not. Enforced by scripts/lib/holdout_policy.py via run_calibration_full.enforce_holdout_year_gate, legitimacy_diagnostics.run_d6_quarantine and audit_keepers. Marker format: "<ISO>": {"declared": "YYYY-MM-DD", "keeper": "<run id frozen for the one-shot score>", "by": "<session/owner>"}.
